reviews.text: As a Kubrick stan, I gotta say, I'm quite disappointed by this film. It took me probably over a decade to finish it... I had seen the first part, told myself I'd eventually finish it and I never went back it till now, I suppose from disinterest... Maybe it was just intuition all along... I'm not as impressed as I typically would be by any of his other films... When there has been violence and overall nasty treatment against women in other Kubrick films, it never felt this gratuitous. It reminded me of something like Goodfellas (that I'm also not as fond of) with the same use of ethnic slurs, violence against women, etc... I get it, it's just a real depiction of how horrible men can be and it's perhaps a criticism against that behavior... Idk... I guess I don't enjoy seeing a whole film about the filthy behavior of men. It's the worst of the Kubrick lot for me.

Si fuera vietnamita y viera una película sobre estadounidenses llorando por lo mucho que sufrieron en la guerra que ellos mismos crearon estaría más que indignado. ¿Es una burla acaso? Estados Unidos tiene dos cosas y fueron bien mostradas en esta película: dinero y descaro. Financiaron una guerra que ni siquiera ganaron, arruinaron y arrebataron vidas de gente inocente y después gastan otros millones en hacer una representación incorrecta, estúpida y mala de los sucesos. Aunque fueron racistas y discriminatorios de igual partes ante cualquier individuo diferente, es lo único real y realmente representativo del país. Eso sí supieron hacer, vaya ironía. 🕴🏻 De todas formas mire la película tras haber sido influenciada en un corto de YouTube, la escena de "El joker" jugando con el dualismo humano al tener dos señales contradictorias en su traje militar, pensé que sería un personaje complejo y se le vería perder o dudar su humanidad. No hay profundidad en su personaje. Toda la película realmente es propaganda estúpida y aburrida, decepcionante si les tenías espectativas.

Even if I feel I'm interested in Vietnam's conflict, I feel like Vietnam's movies are not my type of movie. Needless to say, I can acknowledge that Full Metal Jacket is a great work due to features such as the following ones: - The first part of the film really hits, with the "Sir, yes, Sir" the whole time, the strict routine, and an overwhelming ambience that just catches you in the terror of America. Because the first part is not about Vietnam, but rather about the wickedness of the US (something that also appears in the second half of the film). The stupidity of the conflict is already there, and the last scene, the one where private Pyle spits the now classic "full. metal. jacket.", is great proof of the fact that Americans themselves, in their style of life, cultivated their own defeat – a defeat that, however, has still not arrived neither for them nor us, although its appearance is starting to accelerate. Moving, true, critical, but nothing new – and that's sort of my delusion with all Vietnam's films, including Coppola's. - Still, I think that Kurick's message, although typical and too much spoon-fed, gets straight to the point, and his analysis is spot on. The moment where the soldiers start wondering the reasons for the civilizating mission in Vietnam, they say something like, "We are here to give them freedom, but they do not seem to want it" alongside the "we're killing them in order for them to be free. I don't know. I would prefer to be free rather than dead" it's fantastic. However, Kubrick's point about stupidity and irreflexivity (also, carrying the "born to kill" alongside the sign of peace) goes further, and points at the American contradiction of creating monsters (first part, in the island) while expecting them to only obliterate the enemy – when the only real enemy was themselves. - Even if Kubrick and Coppola's films are critical of the American gaze on the Vietnam War, they are so American-centered. Both films are about American soldiers, without even considering the Vietnamese point of view of the conflict – but rather the American point of view of the Vietnamese point of view. Needless to say, I'm not claiming that Kubrick and Coppola should have done a Vietnamese-centered movie: they are American. Still, the complaint is more about the winners of the narrative: while America arguably lost Vietnam, they even appropriated their own narrative on how badly they lost it. It's not by chance that when one thinks of Vietnam films, everyone thinks of the two mentioned before, and none of the Vietnamese films are counted in that list. Americans are even capable to capitalize their defeats, and to create a narrative of them being the losers which makes them effectively the winners of the narrative. As I stated before, it might be due to the "critical, obvious and american" nature of the critique that I'm not really into Vietnam movies. However, I enjoyed the film, and being able to see it in a cinema room was a great chance that no one should waste.

This was an interesting movie for me to watch. I was born in 1982 so this movie was obviously something that I was never allowed to watch until later. Unfortunately it took me until I was 44 years old before I finally watched the movie. Like everyone else my age I of course could quote lines from the beginning of the movie because I've seen those scenes before and it turned into internet memes over time. Watching the movie in its entirety is actually a very interesting movie. It definitely shows what goes on in the mind of a soldier who's been forced into war that he doesn't really want to be a part of. At first I wasn't sure who the main character was supposed to be until after Pyle goes on the fritz. I wasn't sure where the movie was going to go after that point, but it kind of just shows the troubles and pain of war. It's sad to realize how the lack of communication and empathy caused soldiers to just do whatever to protect their own lives. It's scary. Not sure if it's one I'll ever watch again but it was an interesting watch.

Stanley Kubrick makes this film feel lopsided and disappointing. The opening act at the training camp, following Joker and Pyle's story, is actually quite well done  but it drags on far too long, eating up nearly half the film's runtime. What's most disappointing is the lack of a truly tense atmosphere once the story moves to the Vietnam War itself. Instead of capturing the atmosphere so distinct to Vietnam dense jungle and Viet Cong style traps  Kubrick opts for an urban setting instead, pitting the soldiers against skilled Viet Cong snipers. It ends up feeling more like watching a war against Nazi Germany in Europe than a guerrilla war in Vietnam..

أكثر ما أُعجبني في هذا الفيلم هو عدم إظهار الجنود الأمريكيين كملائكة أو جالبين للحرية وداحضين للشيوعية، بل أظهرهم كما فعلوا تاريخياً: قتل للمدنيين بلا أي استثناء وعدم اهتمام. بالإضافة إلى النصف الأول من الفيلم (أول خمسين دقيقة) في معسكر التدريب، كان نصفاً مثيراً نفسياً بحق، وصادماً بنهايته، وذا أداء تمثيلي مميز من إيرمي على وجه الخصوص، وأيضاً لم أتوقع هكذا بداية في فيلم لكوبريك، فعادةً ما تكون بداية أفلامه بطيئة، لكن هنا لم أأشعر بالوقت. وأما بالنصف الثاني فهنا الفيلم يتحول لعمل قاسٍ غير مكترث بالمشاعر وهذا متوقع نسبياً نظراً لكونه فيلم حرب. وأما بقية الأحداث فليست بالأمر الجلل، أحداث فيلم حرب تقليدية. وأغرب ما في الفيلم هي الموسيقى، لا تدري ما موقعها في فيلم كهذا، تشعر وكأنها موسيقى فيلم كوميدي وليست موسيقى فيلم حرب. آخر قولي عنه: عمل جيد، يستحق المشاهدة لمرة واحدة ككل ولأكثر من مرة لنصفه الأول، محايد في محتواه، أداء تمثيلي ممتاز ككل، ليس مضيعة للوقت.

They are all provided in large quantities. But once they go off to war, it has to restart and rebuild momentum and, even with the addition of the always perfectly cast Adam Baldwin, it just never does.
